STATE_UMBRIA.basis: Documented preindustrial terraced olive agriculture around Assisi and Spoleto; bounded state-level proxy, not measured hectares.

STATE_ROMAGNA.basis: Ferrara/Po delta land reclamation documented in the fourteenth to sixteenth centuries; no twentieth-century drainage assumed.

STATE_VALENCIA.basis: Long-established Horta irrigation; limited local correction within the state.

STATE_LOWER_EGYPT.basis: Nile basin irrigation before mid-nineteenth-century perennial irrigation; excludes modern dams and desert reclamation.

STATE_MIDDLE_EGYPT.basis: Traditional Nile flood-basin cultivation, without modern perennial irrigation.

STATE_UPPER_EGYPT.basis: Traditional Nile flood-basin cultivation constrained to the river valley.

sources.use: Ecological constraint only: desert/arid cultivation requires water. Modern land statistics are not projected backwards.
Arabian oasis farming depends on localized springs and canals; no blanket desert expansion.

notes: All numerical multipliers are explicit conservative gameplay assumptions, not historical measurements of unused farmland.
Original V3 arable land is always the base: rerunning cannot compound increases. Mineral/resource capacities remain unchanged.
Each mapped V3 province gets equal weight; unique source locations within it get equal weight. Neither population size nor an urban population concentration raises the geographic ceiling.
Source development and observed crop/irrigation evidence scale the ceiling. Unemployment demand can select less land but can never raise the ceiling.
Only states with a local remaining employment-capacity shortfall receive extra land. New land remains initially subsistence because productive building levels are unchanged.
No population movement, new commercial farms, invented irrigation projects, ongoing employment guarantees or direct profession rewrites.
